title: The Mystery of the Toynbee Tiles
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the Toynbee Tiles, cut-linoleum messages embedded in asphalt streets across the northeast US and in South America since the mid-1980s. They cover the tiles' text (Arnold J. Toynbee, Kubrick's 2001, resurrecting the dead on Jupiter), the anti-Semitic and media-hostile tags, the link to Arnold Toynbee's ideas and David Mamet's play "4 A.M." inspired by a 1980 Larry King call, the early-1980s TV-interrupting broadcasts and posters in Philadelphia, the "Minority Association" materials, the investigators Justin, Dr. Steve Weinick and Colin Smith and filmmaker John Foy's documentary "Resurrect Dead", the suspect Severino Verna, and the tar-paper and crack-filler method of embedding tiles. A listener mail segment about a paired kidney donation closes the episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the Toynbee tiles
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about a past live show, then Josh introduces the topic from a listener suggestion and describes the tiles' appearance and general message.

segments.title: The tile messages and the tilemaker's anti-Semitic and media-hostile tags
segments.summary: They read the main inscription and smaller tagged messages, including ones about media and journalists, and note that the tags contain anti-Semitic content and that the tilemaker's mental state cannot be established.

segments.title: The documentary Resurrect Dead
segments.summary: They discuss the hour-and-a-half documentary Resurrect Dead, which was hard to find free and which Chuck rented for about four dollars.

segments.title: Arnold Toynbee and the meaning of the tile text
segments.summary: They explain Arnold J. Toynbee's view of rising and falling civilizations and his later Christian-leaning views, and how Kubrick's 2001 and the Jupiter reference connect to the tilemaker's belief in resurrecting the dead.

segments.title: Early broadcasts, posters, and the David Mamet connection
segments.summary: They describe early-1980s TV interruptions by a driver with a high-powered antenna, posters in Philadelphia, and David Mamet's one-act play 4 A.M., which was based on a 1980 Larry King call about resurrecting the dead on Jupiter.

segments.title: Philadelphia origin, the Inquirer, and the Minority Association
segments.summary: They explain how investigators pinpointed a Philadelphia neighborhood, how the tilemaker contacted the Philadelphia Inquirer and reporter Clark Dayleon, and how Minority Association press materials signed by James Morosco revealed the single-person behind the aliases.

segments.title: Suspect Severino Verna and copycat tiles
segments.summary: They describe the investigators' pursuit of Severino Verna, the recluse suspect, the ruled-out alternatives James Morosco and Railroad Jim, the difficulty of separating original from copycat tiles, and the Brazil tile with a Philadelphia address.

segments.title: How the tiles were installed: tar paper and crack filler
segments.summary: They explain the method: a tile wrapped in tar paper and set in asphalt crack filler, which is driven over until the paper wears away and the tile is revealed, as shown by a fresh tile Justin found.

segments.title: Anonymity, the tilemaker's motives, and closing thoughts
segments.summary: They discuss the tiles' ephemeral lifespan, the tilemaker's possible mental illness and privacy, the investigators' approach, and whether the goal was a movement or an art project.

segments.title: Listener mail: phantom kidney
segments.summary: Mackenzie from Maine describes experiencing phantom kidney sensation after donating a kidney through a paired exchange program, and the hosts encourage listeners to look into paired kidney donation.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits for Stuff You Should Know.
